sentences.text: Analyzing AC circuits with sine and cosine differential equations is extremely tedious.
By using Euler's formula: e^(j theta) = cos(theta) + j sin(theta), we transform time-domain sinusoids into complex vectors called Phasors.
A sinusoid v(t) = Vm cos(ω t + phi) becomes the phasor V = Vm ∠ phi.
In the phasor domain, resistors have impedance ZR = R. Inductors have impedance ZL = j ω L, where voltage leads current by 90 degrees.
Capacitors have impedance ZC = 1 / (j ω C) = -j / (ω C), where current leads voltage by 90 degrees.
